tasks.title: Git Archaeology
tasks.reflection: Running git cat-file -p HEAD on my Bayn repo revealed that a commit is not a snapshot of files — it's a pointer. It stores a tree hash, a parent commit hash, and metadata like author and message. When I walked into the tree with git cat-file -p HEAD^{tree}, I could see every file and folder as a list of (type, name, hash) entries. Finally, reading the blob for notes.txt showed just the raw bytes with no metadata. Git builds up a complete picture by chaining three objects — commit → tree → blob — not by copying files.

tasks.title: BLUF Writing
tasks.reflection: Open source is asynchronous. The discipline: lead every message with the conclusion or the ask, then provide context. Three rules: subject line is a contract, show your work not just the conclusion, explicit beats clever.
